newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn divided whether it can afford Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Bonn divided whether it can afford Eurofighter.

text.p: Germany's ruling coalition was divided on Sunday over whether Bonn will be able to afford the new Eurofighter jet in the face of severe spending cuts planned in the 1997 budget.

Juergen Koppelin, a budgetary expert for the Free Democrats (FDP), junior partners in the coalition, dismissed as an "April fool's joke" a claim by Finance Minister Theo Waigel that Bonn would be able to find the money for the four-nation project.

Sources close to the defence ministry said Defence Minister Volker Ruehe, a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, was also less optimistic than Waigel about the availability of funds for the aircraft.
Waigel, in an interview with Bild am Sonntag newspaper, said: "It will be difficult, but the Bosnia mission and the decision to procure the Eurofighter are possible with this budget."

The Eurofighter was needed to replace the air force's Phantom jets, now more than 40 years old, and more than 6.5 billion marks had already been invested in the project since 1985, said Waigel, a member of Kohl's Bavarian sister party, the CSU.
The jet is being built jointly by British Aerospace, which has a 37.5 percent share, Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa) with 30 percent, Italy's Alenia with 19.5 percent and Spain's Casa with 13 percent.
Ruehe said on Friday the military was in deep financial difficulties due to Bonn's effort to meet tight spending limits imposed by the Maastricht Treaty on European Union.

Defence spending will be cut by an additional 200 million marks next year under a deal reached by the coalition on Friday to save a further three billion marks and help make up for an expected shortfall in tax revenues.

While the defence cuts are well below savings imposed on other ministries, experts have warned that they threaten the effectiveness of an army falling behind in maintaining basic equipment -- at a time when it is seeking to play a greater military role in peacekeeping missions.
Ruehe said last month Bonn had a very firm commitment to buying 180 Eurofighters.
